issues.title: Test the Modules video on a real iPhone and Mac
issues.question: Does the Modules video play in Safari on an iPhone and a Mac?
issues.impact: Cloudflare Pages assets ignore Range requests, so data/v2/public/_worker.js answers them for /videos/*, the way Lazurio answers its guide videos. Playback itself was not tested in any browser: the test browser has no H.264 and the build machine has no other browser. The poster and the five captions in the figure keep the page complete without the video.
options: Test on a real iPhone and Mac before publication.
Publish and test on the preview afterwards, since the page stays complete without the video.

issues.title: Align the documentation lockup after the Lazurio logo direction is finalized
issues.question: Which final Lazurio lockup should the documentation header use after the in-progress product identity is approved?
issues.impact: The first release safely uses the text title and the approved favicon. It must not present a working lockup direction as final brand identity.
options: Keep the text title until the design-system owner publishes a final asset.
Adopt the approved asset in a later scoped visual update with browser parity checks.

issues.title: Complete post-migration Cloudflare hardening
issues.question: What reviewed sequence should enable DNSSEC and move eligible lazurio.ai hostnames from DNS-only resolution to Cloudflare proxying now that the authoritative cutover has converged?
issues.impact: Cloudflare now owns authoritative DNS and public resolver convergence was verified on 2026-08-26. DNS-only records preserve the previous network path and do not add Cloudflare proxy, WAF or origin shielding to the dashboard or current apex. Enabling proxying before origin TLS and rollback are verified could interrupt service; DNSSEC still requires a separately reviewed, end-to-end activation.
options: Recommended: enable DNSSEC through Cloudflare and WEDOS with end-to-end validation, then proxy the dashboard only after strict origin TLS and a direct-origin protection path are verified.
Keep the dashboard DNS-only until Cloudflare Tunnel or an origin firewall allowlist prevents bypassing the proxy.
Replace the current apex and wildcard only in the separate Lazurio website rollout; do not combine that content cutover with DNS security hardening.

issues.title: Upgrade the Astro runtime family after dependency-alert reachability review
issues.question: Can one reviewed static-site upgrade remove all 18 current GitHub dependency alerts without regressing the deployed Cloudflare Pages contract?
issues.impact: Live GitHub readback on 2026-08-31 identifies 17 Astro advisories and one @astrojs/cloudflare advisory. The replacement draft moves to patched Astro 7.2.9 with its matching official integrations, removes the unused runtime adapter from this static site, preserves the existing accessibility Markdown transform and validates the Pages 302 redirect through local Pages emulation. It remains in progress until the replacement PR is reviewed and merged.
options: Recommended: review and merge the prepared static-site upgrade, then verify that GitHub closes all 18 alerts on the default branch.
Keep the vulnerable runtime temporarily only with an advisory-by-advisory reachability assessment and an explicit short expiry.

issues.title: Re-verify the five Microsoft 365 Copilot sources before their review date

Retire a source the documentation no longer needs and remove its citations.

issues.title: Give people a clickable way to name a new device, and let the Admin set the name at approval
issues.question: How does a device get its `<login>-<device>` name when no person-facing step may use a command line?
issues.impact: Tailscale names a node after the system hostname; on phones that is usually only the manufacturer or model. Tailscale for Android 1.104.5 has no name setting (checked in the app on 2026-11-03), and Tailscale documents no clickable name setting for iOS, macOS or Windows; the only documented ways are the CLI flag and the Hostname system policy. guide/tailscale-add-device therefore asks people to tell the Admin the wanted name and says the guide does not yet describe how the Admin sets it.
options: Proposed: the Admin types the agreed name in Dashboard when approving, and the approval sets it on the node; until then the system name stays.

Proposed: Dashboard offers a personal settings file (an Apple configuration profile on macOS, a registry file on Windows) with LoginURL and Hostname, opened by double-click. Needs verification that the policies apply with Headscale and do not lock the device to one tailnet.
Accept the system name and show the owner and device kind next to it in Dashboard.
decision_needed_for: the Device name section and Admin check 3 of guide/tailscale-add-device

issues.title: Confirm that Dashboard shows the login server address and the device approval before the add-device guide is published
issues.question: Does the released Dashboard show a person their Organization's Headscale login server address, and does an Admin approve waiting devices there (today through a reviewed batch change)?
issues.impact: Since 2026-11-05 guide/tailscale-add-device no longer says that Dashboard shows the login server or that Admins approve devices in Dashboard: the Admin gives the address, and approval goes through the network administrator's managed procedure (Lazurio Platform v0.1.20 agent manual). The Dashboard approval and the approval service are described as the target of the access model (decision 0192). Once they ship and are verified, the guide can say so.
options: Publish after the Dashboard change ships and re-read it.
Publish now with the Admin as the source of the address, and add Dashboard once it ships.

issues.title: Windows has no clickable way to enter the Organization's login server
issues.question: How does a person on Windows join their Organization's tailnet without a command line?
issues.impact: Tailscale's documentation says the Windows app cannot add a custom control server in its interface; the documented alternatives are the CLI and the LoginURL registry value. Since 2026-11-05 (Matěj Suchánek's decision, recorded in AGENTS.md as the one exception to the no-terminal rule) the guide gives Windows readers one PowerShell line, shown click by click with labelled illustrative mockups, and a copyable prompt for their own agent. That still asks people to use PowerShell, and the mockups are not screenshots of a real Windows computer.
options: Proposed (recommended): a signed Windows app "Připojit k Organizaci" from Moje zařízení that installs Tailscale if needed and opens the Organization's sign-in without a restart or a command (HumanAndMachine-ai/Dashboard#463).

Proposed: Dashboard offers a ready registry file with LoginURL (and Hostname) for the person's Organization; it takes effect only after a restart of the Tailscale service and locks the computer to one server.
Interim in place since 2026-11-05: one PowerShell line with illustrated steps and an agent prompt.
Replace the illustrative mockups with screenshots from a Windows 11 test machine once one exists.
decision_needed_for: the end of the AGENTS.md exception for Windows

issues.title: Add own screenshots for iPhone and macOS to the add-device guide
issues.question: Where can the iPhone and macOS steps be photographed without a signed-in account and without personal data on screen?
issues.impact: The Android steps have own screenshots from Tailscale 1.104.5. iPhone and macOS have none: Tailscale's documentation images carry no licence that allows reuse, so the guide links to them, and the available Mac is a personal machine whose screen may show private data. The macOS Option-click path (Debug → Custom Login Server → Add Account…) comes from the Headscale documentation and is unverified in the current app.
options: Take them on a test iPhone and a test Mac with no Tailscale account.
Have the reviewer take them on their own devices, cropped to the Tailscale window, before publication.
decision_needed_for: the iPhone and macOS sections of guide/tailscale-add-device

issues.title: Update the app connections page and one Tailscale sentence so that nine expired sources can be renewed
issues.question: Who updates environment-app-connections (en, cs) to today's product, and the sentence of guide/tailscale that says the apps of a Remote Environment work only inside a tailnet?
issues.impact: The re-verification of 2026-11-05 renewed 12 of the 21 sources due by 2026-11-08. Nine no longer support their pages, so their review windows were not moved: eight of environment-app-connections, due 2026-11-06, and lazurio-environment-network-decisions of guide/tailscale, due 2026-11-08. The content check therefore fails every pull request from 2026-11-07 until the pages change. What changed: decision 0162 gained eight addenda from 2026-10-08 to 2026-10-27 (Integrations, one own Composio organization per Organization, a team account on a Team Environment, ChatGPT apps off by default); decision 0175 replaced operator with user on 2026-10-21; the catalog gained executor and bitwarden and no longer offers gogcli on a work Remote Environment; the Launchpad now sets the Organization's Composio organization itself; LazurioPlatform issues 40 and 45 hold answers from 2026-10-07 that the page still calls open; decisions 0146 and 0154 were amended by decision 0213, so an Organization in public DNS mode reaches its Environments without a tailnet.
options: Update both pages in one reviewed pull request, re-pin the nine sources to the public decision register and the current LazurioPlatform documents, and renew them. Recommended: it is the only way the page stays true.
Keep the sources expired and accept that no documentation pull request passes the check until the pages are updated.
decision_needed_for: the section Why Tailscale of guide/tailscale (en, cs)

issues.title: At the first pilot, verify the code exchange without a secret on an HTTPS return address with "Allow public client flows" off
issues.question: Does a customer tenant exchange the sign-in code with PKCE and no client secret on an Environment's HTTPS callback registered under the platform "Mobile and desktop applications", while "Allow public client flows" stays off?
issues.impact: Step 3 of microsoft-365 (en, cs) tells IT to register every callback under "Mobile and desktop applications" and to leave "Allow public client flows" off, because Microsoft describes that switch for flows without a redirect URI, such as the device code flow. Microsoft's redirect URI page also says that an app with one or more redirect URIs needs a public client flow configuration. On the owner's decision of 2026-11-17 the text stays as it is. On 22 October 2026 Lazurio's own test tenant exchanged the code without a secret on an Environment's HTTPS callback (LazurioPlatform issue 596, decision F42 addendum (c) point 10), but the public record does not say whether the switch was off there. If a customer tenant refuses the exchange with the switch off, for example by asking for a client secret, step 3 is wrong for every Organization that follows it.
options: Run the check at the first pilot with an assigned test user and the switch off: connect through the Environment's HTTPS callback, confirm that the exchange and later refreshes succeed without a secret, then record the result on microsoft-365 and in LazurioPlatform's company app section. Recommended: it proves the documented setting on the kind of tenant it is meant for.
Repeat the check on Lazurio's own test tenant with the switch confirmed off before the pilot, so that the first Organization does not meet a failure.

issues.title: The add-device guide and Lazurio's agent manual disagree on who sets a device's `<login>-<device>` name
issues.question: Should guide/tailscale-add-device follow the agent manual of Lazurio Platform v0.1.22, in which the agent on the person's computer sets the `<login>-<device>` name on the device before approval, or should the product change to match the guide, in which nobody on the device sets it?
issues.impact: Since #68 (17 November 2026) the guide tells the person's agent not to change the device name ("do not use `--hostname`"), says that today the Organization Admin sets the name with the network operator at approval, and calls a `-1` suffix normal, to be adjusted by the Admin. The agent manual of Lazurio Platform v0.1.22, unchanged on main (`src/folder/manual.ts`, Adding a computer to a tailnet, steps 4 and 5), tells the agent on the source computer to pass `--hostname=<name>` with `--login-server` at first connection, to fix the wrong name of a device that is not yet approved with `tailscale set --hostname`, never to run `headscale nodes rename` on the Conglomerate Host, and to treat a `-1` suffix as not success. The GEN3 record `manual/operator-machine-access.md` and servers-conglomerate-host also say that the name is set on the device itself. No public source says that the Admin sets the name at approval; issue-2026-11-03-001 lists it only as a proposal. Agents with a Lazurio Folder and agents following the guide get opposite instructions. The source lazurio-device-node-names (due 2026-12-03) stays expired until this is decided.
options: Align the guide with the released product for computers: the Windows and Mac prompts set the `<login>-<device>` name on the device before approval, as the agent manual says; the sentence about the Admin setting the name today and the `-1` line follow the manual; phones keep the system's name until issue-2026-11-03-001 is resolved. Recommended: documentation does not redefine runtime behaviour, and nothing changes on servers.

Keep the guide's flow without renaming: replace the unsourced sentence with the gap (the guide does not set the name yet; Lazurio's rule sets it on the device; a clickable way is missing, issue-2026-11-03-001), and propose in LazurioPlatform that the agent manual stop requiring `--hostname` for devices added by the guide.

Change the product: the Organization Admin sets the name at approval (option 1 of issue-2026-11-03-001). This needs a LazurioPlatform decision, because the manual forbids renaming on the Conglomerate Host today; until it ships, the guide states the gap.
decision_needed_for: the Device name paragraph, the `-1` line and the agent details for Windows and macOS in guide/tailscale-add-device (en, cs)

issues.title: Decide whether the public pages keep the GEN3 five-step order for new connections, which LazurioPlatform's Folder leaves out
issues.question: Should Lazurio's public documentation still present the order official MCP server, official CLI, Composio, reviewed open-source MCP server or CLI, supervised browser, from the GEN3 Root's external application standard, as Lazurio's current guidance for a connection that Apps → Integrations does not offer?
issues.impact: environment-app-connections, data-access-security, public-evidence, deployment-operations (step 4) and lazurio-vs-microsoft-copilot (en, cs) present the order as Lazurio's standard and link to the GEN3 Root manual, a GEN3 record since decisions 0225 and 0226. LazurioPlatform deliberately leaves it out of the Folder (`src/folder/manual.ts` at v0.1.22: "The Root's order for a new connection is left out: it puts MCP before the tool and adds paths that are no Integration's."), so agents in an Environment are never told it; LazurioPlatform issue 757 still lists it as open. data-access-security and public-evidence also link to revision 6416d27 instead of the source's pin, and public-evidence's sentence that ChatGPT apps are off is not in that revision. The Composio prompt on guide/tool-connections asks the agent to start the connection itself, which the GEN3 standard and the agent manual at v0.1.22 ("Never start a connection yourself, neither in Composio nor in Executor.") forbid in Lazurio; it is corrected together with this decision. Everything else these pages draw from the source holds against LazurioPlatform v0.1.22. The source lazurio-external-apps-current (due 2026-12-06) stays expired until this is decided.
options: Describe today's rules from LazurioPlatform (a custom MCP server goes into Executor only on the user's instruction, with the provider's official server first; no own integration without the user's decision; the forbidden list of decision 0162) and keep the five-step order only as a labelled GEN3 record, or drop it; retitle the source as a GEN3 record pinned to the root's main and align the links. Recommended: the pages then describe what the product does today, and LazurioPlatform is the authority since decision 0225.

Keep the order as Lazurio's recommendation and ask LazurioPlatform to add it to the Folder (issue 757); until then only the link pins change, and the pages keep promising a rule that agents in an Environment are not given.
Remove the order and the GEN3 link from every page and cite only environment-app-connections and LazurioPlatform's Integrations.
decision_needed_for: deployment-operations (en, cs) step 4, lazurio-vs-microsoft-copilot (en, cs) and the Composio prompt on guide/tool-connections (en, cs)
